newsitem.title: USA: Triton proven reserves up 148 pct.
newsitem.headline: Triton proven reserves up 148 pct.

text.p: Triton Energy Ltd said Tuesday its proved oil and natural gas reserves increased 148 percent to 308 million barrels of oil equivalent (boe) during 1996.
The total compares with 124 million boe at the end of 1995, adjusted for asset sales, the company said.
In addition, Triton said, its resource base has increased 133 percent to 836 million barrels as of December 31, compared with 476 million boe at year-end 1995.
The 836 million boe consists of 2.973 trillion cubic feet of natural gas and 340 million barrels of oil and condensate.
This is the first time Triton has reported its resource base, the company noted. This total was also reported Monday by Mobil Corp.

Triton explained its resource base provides a more complete picture of current assets and future potential. It includes proved and probable oil and natural gas reserves, as well as other quantities of discovered oil and natural gas that ultimately may be commercially recoverable.

Triton said it has used recognized petroleum industry standards and practices, including Securities and Exchange Commission standards for proved reserves, to define the components of its resource base, which does not include reserves that may be discovered by future exploratory drilling.

"Our sizable resource base and significant increase in proved reserves are evidence of our exploration achievements on Block A-18 in the Gulf of Thailand, as well as our continued success in appraising and developing the Cusiana and Cupiagua fields in Colombia," said chief executive Tom Finck.
"Today, we are positioned for significant growth in both production and cash flow as we invest in the development of our resource base, which is largely undeveloped."
